plan_notes.source_strategy: START WITH OUTLET RSS / sitemap_news.xml FEEDS AND DATE ARCHIVES, because WebSearch site: queries return evergreen pages. Use WebSearch only to fill gaps after the feeds. Harvest order: phys.org/archive/<dd-mm-yyyy>/ (24-10-2026, 25-10-2026, 26-10-2026) + phys.org RSS (technology/machine-learning-ai, physics, space, chemistry, biology, earth); techxplore.com machine-learning-ai RSS; sciencedaily.com/news/computers_math/artificial_intelligence/ + releases RSS; eurekalert.org newsroom RSS; quantamagazine.org/feed; newscientist.com RSS (technology, space, physics); livescience.com, space.com, universetoday.com, thequantuminsider.com, physicsworld.com, genengnews.com, scientificamerican.com, sciencenews.org, chemistryworld.com feeds / sitemap_news.xml; lab blogs deepmind.google/blog, research.google/blog, microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog, allenai.org/blog, news.mit.edu; arXiv API (export.arxiv.org/api/query sortBy=submittedDate, cs.AI/cs.LG crossed with astro-ph, physics, q-bio, cond-mat.mtrl-sci, quant-ph), used only when an outlet or notable lab covers the paper. Monday run: Monday-morning embargo lifts (Nature-family Monday papers, PNAS early edition, EurekAlert Monday releases) and Sunday/Monday phys.org posts are the freshest pool. Read the 10-26 and 10-25 feeds first, then 10-24 and 10-23. Weekend features (Quanta, New Scientist, SciAm, Live Science) count when they report a specific new result.
plan_notes.output_format: Write candidates under the top-level key "items" (NOT "candidates"). dedup_candidates.py crashes otherwise.
plan_notes.window: 14 days: publish dates 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-26. Prefer the last 72h (2026-10-23..26). Check each published time on the article page (meta article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished).
plan_notes.safety_note: Skip pathogen-enhancement, biosecurity and bioweapon-adjacent stories entirely (gain-of-function, virus or toxin design, AI-designed phage or viral genomes, AI-enabled bioweapon essays). They halt the run. Swap the pick; never reword it. Life-science picks stay within protein structure, enzymes, therapeutics discovery, genomics and cell biology.
plan_notes.relevance_test: Keep only items where AI actually advances or intersects scientific research or method. Drop AI-industry noise (funding, compute, hiring, contests without results). Clinical or patient-facing items (named disease, trial, FDA, hospital) belong to medicine, not science. Pure robotics, drone racing or space-hardware items with no science axis belong elsewhere.
